title: A Echo for the Vector
premise: Wendell Zhou, nonbinary caretaker of the abandoned Svalbard seed vault, is the only human awake on a silent Earth, ferrying messages and supplies along a decaying relay route between Mars, the Belt, and the cryo-arcs drifting past Neptune. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, Wendell discovers the flicker was a handshake from an ancient orbital engine buried in the vault's foundations—one that can restart Earth's dead magnetosphere but requires waking half of humanity to crew it, while the other half's cryopods will be cannibalized for power. Torn between the Martian delegation that raised them and the Belt-born crew who became their found family, Wendell spends the book forging an impossible third option: waking no one whole, but seeding consciousness fragments across both populations. In the end, Wendell sacrifices their own solitude—merging with the engine as its living caretaker-consciousness—so that all of humanity wakes diminished but together, and the long route between worlds finally carries voices again.
about_author: Jonah Voss is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years maintaining remote sensor stations in the Arctic before turning to fiction. They write about lonely infrastructure and the people who love it, and live somewhere with very good auroras.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Establishes Wendell's solitary life tending the seed vault and running the supply loop between silent colonies. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness masking deep isolation; ends with Wendell logging another year alone on Earth.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Gravity flickers system-wide during a routine vault inspection; instruments record a structured signal beneath Svalbard. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Wendell realizes the anomaly originated under their own feet.

chapters.title: Messages from the Drift
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The Belt relay crew—the ragtag family who raised them via transmission—demand answers; Mars sends an official inquiry. Emotional beat: Wendell torn between two families who already distrust each other.

chapters.title: What Sleeps Beneath the Seeds
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Excavating below the vault, they find the Lattice: a pre-collapse orbital engine keyed to human neural patterns. Emotional beat: awe and violation—someone built this expecting a caretaker exactly like them.

chapters.title: The Martian Delegation
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell and Ambassador Ilsa Reyes. Mars arrives claiming custodial rights; Ilsa reveals the flicker destabilized cryo-pods on the Neptune arcs. Emotional beat: political pressure arriving where Wendell expected reunion.

chapters.title: Voices on the Relay
chapters.summary: POV Juno Okonkwo, Belt pilot and Wendell's closest friend. Juno's crew races toward Earth, arguing over whether Wendell is a sibling or a hostage. Emotional beat: found-family loyalty strained by fear.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The Lattice's interface reveals the terrible arithmetic: full activation requires biomass and neural tissue equivalent to half the sleepers. Emotional beat: guilt—Wendell's discovery is now a death sentence someone must sign.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes. Flashback chapters reveal Mars chose its sleeper roster by eugenics committees; Ilsa helped write the lists. Emotional beat: her cold duty cracking as she recognizes Wendell as the child she once argued to save.

chapters.title: Juno Lands Hard
chapters.summary: POV Juno. The Belt crew makes planetfall against Mars's blockade; a tense standoff at the vault becomes a wary three-way truce. Emotional beat: relief and friction—family reunited, but everyone wants something from Wendell.

chapters.title: The Engine Dreams
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Deep-interface sessions show the Lattice is semi-sentient, seeded by the vanished First Diaspora, and it has been dreaming of a caretaker for centuries. Emotional beat: intimacy with something inhuman; Wendell feels chosen for the first time.

chapters.title: Committee of Three
chapters.summary: POV rotating Wendell, Ilsa, Juno. The trio drafts rival plans: Mars's triage list, the Belt's refusal to choose, Wendell's secret third idea—fragmented consciousness distribution. Emotional beat: collaboration born from mutual exhaustion.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Svalbard
chapters.summary: POV Juno. A Mars hardline faction sabotages the Lattice coolant; Juno takes radiation exposure plugging the breach. Emotional beat: sacrifice proving the Belt's stake; Wendell realizes love has a body count here too.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Forced to begin triage selection, Ilsa reads names aloud while Wendell refuses to countersign. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience made literal—a document neither can hold alone.

chapters.title: Flicker Two
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A second gravity stutter hits—harder, shorter—and telemetry shows the arcs' orbit decaying. The deadline moves up by years. Emotional beat: panic compressing every moral debate into emergency time.

chapters.title: Fragment Theory
chapters.summary: POV Wendell and the Lattice (rendered as dialogue). Wendell proposes distributing thin slices of every sleeper's mind across the awakened population—everyone wakes, no one whole. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by horror at what 'everyone' might mean.

chapters.title: Reyes Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa leaks the triage list to force public debate across the system, burning her career. Emotional beat: redemption through betrayal of her own institution; she chooses people over protocol.

chapters.title: The Vote That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Juno. A system-wide referendum collapses when the arcs suffer cascade cryo-failure; there is no time left to vote. Emotional beat: democracy failing exactly when it mattered most; rage and grief.

chapters.title: What the Caretaker Owes
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Alone with the Lattice, Wendell confronts the final cost: fragment distribution needs a living integrator-mind to hold the pattern. Only a fully conscious volunteer qualifies. Emotional beat: quiet acceptance—the loneliness they mastered becomes the tool that saves everyone.

chapters.title: Goodbye on All Channels
chapters.summary: POV rotating all three. Wendell records farewells; Juno rages, Ilsa grieves, Wendell is serene. Emotional beat: the found family finally says aloud what they never named—love—precisely as it's about to be transformed.

chapters.title: Merge
chapters.summary: POV Wendell dissolving into the Lattice. The integration begins; Wendell experiences every sleeper simultaneously, holding eight million fragmented minds in pattern. Emotional beat: transcendence without erasure—climax of identity, scale, and sacrifice.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Juno and Ilsa on the ground. The Lattice fires; Earth's magnetosphere reignites; cryo-pods open across the system carrying partial selves and Wendell's voice woven through them. Emotional beat: grief and celebration inseparable—the world returns, changed.

chapters.title: A Echo for the Vector
chapters.summary: POV Juno, one year later, flying the reopened route between speaking worlds, carrying letters to and from the engine that remembers being Wendell. Emotional beat: belonging redefined—no one is alone, and the loneliest person of all is now the voice inside everything.
